images.title: Images and illustrations
images.intro: Input formats, reuse, independent crops, and fitting images into frames. All sample assets are generated in this repository.

png: Import a PNG at a specified physical width while preserving the complete image on the page.
jpeg: Place a JPEG in the same layout to inspect the rendered appearance of a lossy image.
svg: Import a safe subset of SVG. The artwork remains vector content in SVG and PDF exports.
tiff-gray: Import a single-page, single-channel 8-bit TIFF generated by the repository scripts.
reuse: Place one image definition twice at different widths; each placement has independent settings.
crop: Crop the right placement from the source while the left placement still shows the full image.
fit-contain: Scale proportionally to show the entire image inside the frame, leaving space when needed.
fit-cover: Scale proportionally until the image fills the frame, clipping any overflow.
fit-stretch: Scale width and height independently to demonstrate a nonuniform fit.

positioning.title: Positioning and layers
positioning.intro: Build relationships with placement anchors; rotation, opacity, and add order then determine the final drawing.

anchors: Put a dot at each of a rectangle's nine anchors to show their actual positions.
relative: Anchor each later block to an earlier placement so the chain follows changes.
dependent-size: Override the first placement's width and let a later object follow the new anchor position.
rotation: Rotate a rectangle around its center; a marker shows the rotation origin.
opacity: Overlap two rectangles; the foreground placement's opacity applies only to that placement.
drawing-order: Later add calls paint on top, as visible where opaque blocks overlap.
geometry-anchors: Select layout-box corners, geometric paths and ink boundaries on rounded rectangles, ellipses and thick arrows.
path-locations: Source nodes and controls, arc-length versus parameter points, intervals and tangent-frame offsets.
chart-parts: Domain endpoints on a reversed axis, vertical spines, label bounds and data-coordinate anchors.

containers.title: Groups and components
containers.intro: Organize objects in local coordinates and reuse layouts through groups and local modules.

group-local: Position a child relative to another placement inside a group, then place the whole group on the page.
group-nested: Nest one group inside another, then scale and rotate the outer placement.
group-reuse: Place the same group at two sizes without changing its original definition.
module-import: Import a card function from a neighboring .lay module to create two independent placements.

shapes.title: Shapes and drawing
shapes.intro: Basic shapes, paths, fills, dashes, compound outlines, and visible-outline fusion.

rect: Set corner radius, fill, and stroke independently on a rectangle.
ellipse: Use different width and height to show the fill, stroke, and bounding box.
line-arrow: Draw a straight line and a diagonal arrow in the same coordinate system.
polygon-polyline: A polygon closes automatically; a polyline follows only the supplied points.
arc-sector: Compare an open arc with a closed sector at the same radius.
star-ring: Inner and outer radii shape the star; the ring keeps its central hole transparent.
path-commands: Join straight, quadratic, cubic, and elliptical-arc segments into one path.
evenodd-hole: Outer and inner subpaths use even-odd fill to leave a transparent hole.
linear-gradient: Fill a rectangle diagonally with multiple color stops.
radial-gradient: Control the transition inside an ellipse with a center and radius.
dashes: Compare one and multiple dash-gap length pairs on two lines.
outlines: Create single, double, and triple outlines from the same color and line width.
fuse: Join the visible outlines of a rectangle and line into a new vector path.
fuse-angled: Angled line on a straight edge
Join lines sloping up and down to rectangle edges and inspect both continuous fillets.
fuse-curved: Angled line on a curved edge
Join lines to an ellipse and a free Bézier curve, inspecting the curved seams.
fuse-outline-edge: Line joined to a hollow edge
Join a diagonal line at the midpoint of a hollow rectangle's right edge while preserving its hole.
fuse-outline-corner: Line joined to a hollow corner
Join a diagonal line at a hollow rectangle's upper-right corner and preserve both contours.
line-endpoints: Six head shapes, zero-length heads, translucent junctions and curve direction.
colors-alpha: HEX, RGB, HSV and OKLCH share alpha and export rules.

typography.title: Text and formulas
typography.intro: Fonts, wrapping, colored spans, inline formulas, and standalone formulas.

font: Use installed system families or font files with ordered fallback for Latin and Chinese text across all three export backends.
wrap-align: Place the same paragraph at two widths; centered line counts change with width.
spans: Override color and size separately for spans in one line.
inline-formula: Put a formula span on the same line as ordinary text.
display-formula: Center a standalone formula; the PDF retains its original LaTeX source.

scripting.title: Scripting and calculations
scripting.intro: Variables, units, functions, and control flow within the restricted .lay language.

units-builtins: Write the results of append, len, min, max, abs, and str directly onto the image.
control-flow: Combine a user function with for, while, and if to compute visible text.
dictionaries: Iterate dictionaries in insertion order, update independent values, and combine layouts with enumerate and zip.

plots.title: Scientific data plots
plots.intro: Cartesian, polar and radar plots with fixed physical data areas and manually placed panels and decorations.

multi-axes-breaks: Three vertical axes have different breaks and physical gaps; the horizontal axis is independently broken. Edit the fixed data rectangle and axis offsets directly.
statistics: Explicit bar positions and stacking baselines, steps, histogram density, ECDF, boxes and violins. A constant violin sample intentionally shows its median and warns.
shared-colors: Nonuniform heatmap cells, grid contours and per-point color/size/opacity share one centered diverging scale. The standalone horizontal colorbar is positioned manually.
inset: Separate plots, an arrow and text are composed with existing anchors inside one group. The main symlog plot and the linear inset retain independent mappings.
polar-directions: Compare mathematical angles with north/clockwise orientation; negative radii produce an expected suppressible warning.
polar-errors: Radial/angular errors, hollow markers and physical hatching in a fixed sector.
polar-rose: Periodic bins preserve counts; explicit baselines stack sectors around a physical inner hole.
polar-field: Nonuniform radial cells and periodic contour fields share an independent colorbar.
radar: Explicit indicator ranges retain signed raw units and anchors, alongside a common-scale example.
polar-data: Polar and radar data from Python
NumPy fields/radar arrays persist as hashed JSON; missing adjacent grid cells remain empty.
dictionary-series: Store experimental series in a dictionary and plot them with a loop and a tab10 color cycle.
cmap-presets: Browse the complete Matplotlib 3.11.2 preset collection with native categorical colors.
cmap-scales: Use one cmap handle for heatmap, filled contours, numeric scatter and colorbar.
